بند سابله را شیخ سلمان در جلوی کارون بست تا آب را بالا آورده به جوی قبان برساند و سراسر زمین‌های بخش جنوبی خوزستان را فاریاب و آباد کند (بند بستن شیخ سلمان در جلوی کارون). تاریخ زندیه آن را «نمونه سد اسکندر» نامیده است (لشکرکشی کریم‌خان به خوزستان). کریم‌خان این بند را بشکست، کاری که مؤلف آن از سیاه‌کاری‌های او شمرده است، زیرا بند بستن در خوزستان آیه آبادی شهرها و خرمی کشتزارهاست (لشکرکشی کریم‌خان به خوزستان). میجر کینیرا انگلیسی می‌نویسد اگر کریم‌خان آن را نشکسته بود تا قرن‌ها استوار می‌ایستاد (بند بستن شیخ سلمان در جلوی کارون). پس از آن، شیخ سلمان در پنج سال باقی عمرش دیگر به بستن بند برنخاست و آبادی‌های نتیجه آن بند یکبار دیگر از میان رفت (زینهار خواستن شیخ سلمان از کریم‌خان).

مأمور انگلیسی (روایت کتاب تاریخ روابط سیاسی ایران و انگلیس) - قرن نوزدهم میلادی: شهر محمره را شیخ اعراب کعب بنا نموده است.
کسروی (تاریخ پانصد ساله خوزستان) - قرن‌های پس از اسلام: بیان شهری قدیمی در خوزستان بود که از قرن چهارم (مقدسی) پس از آن نامی از آن نیست و در آخرهای قرن دوازدهم آبادی به نام «محمره» به جای آن پدید می‌آید؛ نخستین بار نام محمره در تاریخچه کعب در زمان شیخ غیث به صورت «کوت المحمره» آمده که دژی بوده و گروهی از کعبیان در آن نشیمن داشته‌اند.

تفاوت: مأمور انگلیسی بنای شهر را به شیخ اعراب کعب نسبت می‌دهد، در حالی که روایت کسروی محمره را ادامه و بازآبادی شهر کهن‌تر «بیان» می‌داند که بعدها دژ کعبیان (کوت المحمره) در آن شکل گرفت؛ بنابراین دو روایت درباره خاستگاه و بانی شهر همخوان نیستند.

- قرارداد ۱۹۱۹ را وثوق‌الدوله با انگلیس بست [2] و در ذی‌القعده ۱۳۳۷ (دسامبر ۱۹۱۹) میان دولت ایران و بریتانیا منعقد شد و مالیه و قشون ایران زیر نظر مستشاران انگلیسی رفت [5].
- در قضایای انحلال پلیس جنوب، دولت بریتانیا مطالبه کرد؛ از جمله صد و سی هزار لیره‌ای که هنگام انعقاد قرارداد ۱۹۱۹ توسط وزیر مالیه صارم‌الدوله اخذ و بین وثوق‌الدوله، صارم‌الدوله و نصرةالدوله تقسیم شده بود، و مجموع مطالبه دو میلیون و کسری لیره بود که دولت ایران آن را نپذیرفت [3].

Veblen concedes the corset impairs the wearer's personal attractions, but this loss is offset by the gain in reputability from her visibly increased expensiveness and infirmity (evidence [1]). It has fallen into disuse among the richest class because a leisure class has grown up wealthy enough that any aspersion of enforced manual employment would be idle, harmless calumny (evidence [4]). It persists among exceptions that are more apparent than real: the wealthy classes of countries with a lower, more archaic industrial structure, and the newly rich in advanced communities who have not yet shed the plebeian canons of taste from their former lower pecuniary grade—e.g., higher social classes of American cities that recently and rapidly rose into opulence (evidence [3]). More broadly, it continues wherever and so long as it serves as evidence of honorific leisure by arguing physical disability in the wearer (evidence [2], [5]).

Mill - On Liberty: Social tyranny—society imposing its own ideas and practices as rules of conduct on dissenters through prevailing opinion and feeling, penetrating deeply into the details of life and "enslaving the soul itself."
Tocqueville - Democracy in America: The tyranny of the majority is more sensibly felt in the manners than in the conduct of society, checking the development of leading characters.

Both see the danger reaching beyond legal/political oppression into social and moral life: Mill emphasizes society's power over individual thought and conscience, while Tocqueville emphasizes its effect on manners and the suppression of independent characters.

Darwin calls it the doctrine of Malthus applied to the whole animal and vegetable kingdoms [1][2]. According to Malthus's Essay, population when unchecked increases in a geometrical ratio, while subsistence increases only in an arithmetical ratio [3][4]. He takes as his rule, based on the United States experience, that unchecked population doubles every twenty-five years [5].

Yes — both uses are caught by the prohibition in Article 5(1)(f).

- Article 5(1)(f) prohibits the placing on the market, the putting into service for this specific purpose, or the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions.
- The only exception in Article 5(1)(f) is where the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons; neither scientific research nor retail staff monitoring qualifies.
- Recital (44) confirms the prohibition covers AI systems intended to detect the emotional state of individuals in workplace situations, and that the exception is limited to systems placed on the market strictly for medical or safety reasons, such as therapeutic use.
- The retailer's use to monitor staff mood in shops is a workplace use, so it is prohibited.
- The lab's putting into service of the system for workers is likewise a workplace emotion-inference use, and no research exemption appears in the cited provisions, so it is also caught unless it falls within the medical or safety exception.

The platform must give the user access to an internal complaint-handling system to contest the removal decision. Under Article 20(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, providers of online platforms must provide recipients of the service with this system for a period of at least six months following the decision. Under Article 20(2), that six-month period starts on the day the recipient is informed about the decision in accordance with Article 16(5) or Article 17. Complaints can be lodged electronically and free of charge (Article 20(1)). The system must be easy to access, user-friendly, and enable sufficiently precise and adequately substantiated complaints (Article 20(3)), and it must not set formal requirements such as referral to specific legal provisions or elaborate legal explanations (recital guidance in [4]).

2. The next remedy is the right to repair or replacement under section 23, which (per section 19(3)) is available for goods that breach the satisfactory quality term.
3. If repair or replacement fails or is unavailable, the consumer then has the right to a price reduction or the final right to reject under section 24 (see section 19(3)(c) and 24(5)).
4. On the burden of proof: under section 19(14), goods that do not conform within six months of delivery are presumed not to have conformed on the day of delivery, so the consumer need not prove the fault existed at delivery.
5. That presumption does not apply if it is established the goods did conform on that day, or if applying it is incompatible with the nature of the goods or how they fail to conform (section 19(15)).

The AI Act relies on the definition of 'personal data' in Union data protection law rather than defining it itself: evidence [4] states that the AI Act does not affect existing Union law governing the processing of personal data, and providers and deployers remain data controllers or processors under that law when their AI systems involve processing personal data. The Data Act (Regulation (EU) 2023/2854), Article 2, point (3), likewise defines 'personal data' by cross-reference to Article 4, point (1), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (the GDPR). However, the actual wording of the GDPR Article 4(1) definition is not contained in the provided evidence, so its content cannot be quoted here.

AI Act (general case) - Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 73: not later than 15 days after becoming aware of the serious incident
GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Article 33: not later than 72 hours after having become aware of the breach

The GDPR's 72-hour deadline is shorter than the AI Act's 15-day deadline (72 hours = 3 days vs 15 days).

UK police force (Part 3, section 35 breach) - higher maximum amount: £17,500,000 (before IP completion day, treated as 20 million Euros per Schedule 21)
EU company (GDPR principles breach) - maximum penalty: 20 million Euros (Article 83(5) of the GDPR, as referenced via the UK GDPR in Schedule 21)

The police force faces the higher maximum amount under section 157(2)(a) for a Part 3 infringement, which is £17,500,000 (equivalent to 20 million Euros before IP completion day), while the EU company faces up to 20 million Euros under Article 83(5) — so the two maxima are effectively the same amount, though expressed in different currencies and subject to different regimes.
